﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ — a questioning of reproach.

﴿So declare openly﴾ O Muhammad ﴿what you are commanded﴾ to do, meaning proclaim it openly and carry it out. ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾. This was before the command to engage in jihad (struggle, here meaning armed fighting).

﴿Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers﴾ — by Our destroying each of them with a calamity. They were: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-'As ibn Wa'il, 'Adi ibn Qays, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 15, verse 96:

﴿Those who set up with Allah another god﴾ is an attribute (ṣifah); and it was said it is a subject (mubtada'), and because it includes the meaning of a conditional (sharṭ), the fā' (fa) entered its predicate (khabar), which is ﴿then they will come to know﴾ the outcome of their affair.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 15, verse 97:

﴿Indeed, We know﴾ — "wa-laqad" (the lam and qad are for emphasis, confirming the matter) — "that your breast is constricted by what they say" — of mockery and denial.
﴿So glorify﴾, combining it with ﴿the praise of your Lord﴾, that is, say: "Glory be to God, and praise be to Him." ﴿And be among those who prostrate﴾, meaning those who pray.
﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾ — death.
